item.title: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković
item.description: The Student List has shown my generation, who protested against the Milošević regime in the 1990s, how we should have done it On Halloween, a few days after a student-led movement swept aside an illiberal, seemingly invincible regime in my native Serbia, I was sitting on the Vienna tram and watched various friendly and malicious monsters getting on and off around me. Witches, devils and unicorns were politely making their way to their respective parties. Not all monsters wear fancy dress. Later that evening, I walked past a Serbian restaurant; in front of it stood a group of grumpy-looking men. They were smoking, spitting and swearing. I recognised the hardened, couldn’t-care-less attitude, the smell of corruption, the penchant for violence. Yet they looked as though their lives were coming to an end. These men are the losers of the revolution that is taking place in Serbia. Their smuggling routes and deals are under threat. Their criminal networks no longer function. Continue reading.

The distinctive quality of his new collection of memoir and essays, Songs from the Firefront, is urgency verging on panic. He’s an elder in his 60s, with limited time to get his messages across before we all go up in flames. Living on the western edge of Australia, Winton has been an eloquent climate-change activist for decades . He has fought, with tenuous success, to protect Ningaloo Reef.
